one_line_description: Shopify is an ecommerce platform that allows developers to build apps and extend its functionality. It provides an API for authentication and various tools for managing store data.
auth_notes: Shopify uses OAuth 2.0 for authentication. Starting April 1, 2026, all public apps will require expiring offline access tokens.

evidence.quote_snippet: To call a Shopify API, your code sends an access token in a request header to authenticate the identity that token represents (your app or a buyer) and authorize what that identity can access.
Shopify uses session tokens - short-lived JWTs - to verify that a request from your app's frontend originates from a valid shop or user.
The GraphQL Admin API is the most common starting point for developers. Accessing it requires the X-Shopify-Access-Token header, with tokens obtained through OAuth or Token Exchange.
Shopify provides three main API surfaces, each with its own authentication method.
This server provides tools for managing products, customers, orders, and more.
